transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-20
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Alvarez (Redwood SE), Sarah Patel (Zenith - Procurement), Tom Briggs (Zenith - Legal), Priya Nair (Zenith - CTO), Liam O'Connor (Zenith - Eng)

Summary:
Maya opened with framing: procurement & legal want final MSA/DPA alignment, SLA appendix details, and internal pricing approvals for a small pilot. Redwood AE+SE walked through SLA options (S0 low-latency vs S1 cost-optimized), data residency and DPA redline items, and pricing tiers for hosted vs dedicated. Customer legal had a few redline items around audit logs, breach notification timing, and indemnity. Action items agreed: Redwood to send redlines, SE to share SLA metrics dashboard and benchmark data, Zenith to return DPA comments, target pilot kickoff mid-Mar.

Topics:
- MSA/DPA redline and turnover timing
- SLAs: uptime, P99 latency targets, credits and remedies
- Pricing approvals: hosted usage vs dedicated reserved capacity pricing
- Vendor onboarding and pilot scope (data access, KPIs)
- Security requirements: SOC 2, KMS, SSO/SAML, retention

Key notes / imperfect auto-transcript: some words garbled (e.g., "KV cache" transcribed as "K-V cash" at times), speaker overlap present.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'll do a quick agenda, then Carlos will jump into the SLA appendix and the benchmark numbers.
[00:18] Sarah: Hi thanks, from procurement side we mainly want to lock the MSA and DPA timelines, and then get final pricing sign-off. We have internal approval meeting next Tuesday so hoping to get things over the fence before then.
[00:32] Tom: From legal, we have a handful of redline priorities: breach notification windows, audit right scope, indemnity cap questions, and subprocessor disclosure frequency. We'll flag the top ones now.
[00:48] Carlos: Great, I'll cover the SLA tradeoffs — we generally have the hosted API with standard SLA 99.9 uptime and P99 latency targets around 450ms for typical gen calls; for dedicated pools you get stronger predictability and can push to lower P99 for a committed throughput. Note those numbers are for our curated models, and of course they vary by sequence length and batch config.
[01:15] Priya: Sorry to interrupt — can you restate the P99 number, we have some real-time inference needs.
[01:22] Carlos: Yeah, P99 ~450ms observed on rNLP-1-small-ish workloads, but if you have long seq or embeddings heavy workload it shifts. For dedicated we can target 200-300ms P99 with reserved capacity and tuning, plus KV cache warmup. (transcription sometimes shows K-V cash).
[02:05] Liam: For the pilot, we plan to run a subset of our customer-facing chat flows, about 5k requests/day, 30T tokens/day peak. Would hosted make sense or should we do a small dedicated pool?
[02:22] Carlos: For that size, hosted is fine for initial pilot — it's cheaper and faster to onboard. If you want tight latency SLOs or data isolation we can propose a small dedicated pool. We can price both and show delta.
[03:10] Maya: On the MSA/DPA front, we pushed a draft last week. Tom, did you and team review?
[03:20] Tom: Yes, we did a quick pass. Main asks: reduce breach notif window from 72 to 48 hours, add quarterly subprocessor list updates, and request audit rights to be exercised once a year with a third-party auditor. Also question on data deletion certs for pilot.
[03:40] Maya: Ok we'll take those. On breach notif, we can accept 48 in most cases but need carveouts for zero-day infra events — Carlos, is that operationally reasonable?
[03:49] Carlos: 48 is tight but operationally we can commit to initial notif and then detailed follow-up within that window; full forensic report may take longer, we should call that out in the DPA.
[04:15] Tom: Also indemnity language — we'd like to see a cap tied to fees over last 12 months instead of a fixed number.
[04:22] Maya: We can discuss cap floor/ceiling; typical enterprise asks we can negotiate, we'll have legal run a clean redline.
[04:40] Sarah: Pricing — can you walk through the hosted vs dedicated numbers again? I forwarded the spreadsheet but want to make sure we all on same page.
[04:51] Maya: Sure; short version: hosted usage is pay-as-you-go per token; estimated for your pilot ~ $X/month (placeholder) — dedicated is a monthly reserved commitment but reduces per-token cost by about 40-60% depending on utilization. We'll send a redline of the pricing worksheet with the exact bands.
[05:30] Priya: Important for us: KMS integration — we need customer-managed keys for production. Is that supported in private/dedicated?
[05:40] Carlos: Yes, we support KMS/HSM for Private deployments and Dedicated can support bring-your-own-key for certain plans. For hosted, we offer tenant key isolation and an encrypted-at-rest model but not full BYOK in the basic plan. We'll include the matrix in the docs.
[06:10] Tom: Also SSO and RBAC — we need SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. Any known gaps?
[06:20] Maya: SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning supported, RBAC is configurable in the console. For onboarding we'll provide a runbook and an SSO test account.
[07:05] Carlos: Back to SLAs — the appendix has remedies: service credits tiered by monthly uptime percentage; for P99 latency misses we offer investigatory credits and operational remediation, not straight dollar credits usually. For Dedicated we can offer stricter remedies.
[07:36] Sarah: Our procurement prefers dollar credits, but legal is okay with tiered credits if there's transparency on metrics.
[07:50] Tom: We need the metric definitions to be explicit — what counts as downtime, how is P99 measured (synthetic vs production), and the sampling window.
[08:05] Carlos: Agreed — we'll add definitions: synthetic client-side probes + server-side telemetry, 5-minute windows for uptime, P99 computed from production request latencies excluding warmup and maintenance windows. We'll share the exact query for the dashboard.
[09:12] Liam: One operational question: what telemetry do we expose? Traces, token-level cost, request ids?
[09:22] Carlos: We expose per-request telemetry, trace ids, per-token billing breakdown in the console, and a logs export. We can also add webhook hooks for certain infra events.
[10:00] Maya: Any competitor concerns? I know you evaluated other vendors.
[10:08] Priya: We looked at Anthropic for safety and OpenAI for model quality; main reason we're talking to Redwood is the cost predictability and the hybrid deployment options.
[10:22] Maya: Good to know. We'll make sure to highlight our differentiate on cost controls and rollout tooling.
[11:00] Sarah: Timeline — procurement has an approval meeting next Tue as I said, pricing sign-off required that day. If legal has redline back in a week we could push to pilot in early March.
[11:15] Tom: We'll try to turn DPA comments in by 2026-02-27.
[11:25] Maya: Great. For the pilot scope, can we confirm KPIs? Carlos, propose some standard pilot success metrics.
[11:32] Carlos: Typical pilot KPIs: P99 latency under X ms for 95% of flows, error rate under 0.5%, cost per 1k tokens under $Y, and qualitative feedback on output quality. We'll give a sample template.
[12:05] Priya: For quality checks, we'll provide a 2000-prompt eval set. Does Redwood run regression evals?
[12:13] Carlos: Yes we have a regression eval harness tied to specific prompt sets; we can run before/after comparisons. We'll share the eval checklist and example reports.
[13:00] Sarah: On data residency — our customers in EU demand EU-only storage. Does Redwood hosted offer region-specific data residency?
[13:10] Maya: Yes, we can pin to EU regions for hosted accounts; Private deployment gives full control. We'll document the region options.
[13:45] Tom: On auditability, we want exportable audit logs for two years. Is that supported?
[13:54] Carlos: Audit logs are available and retention configurable; standard retention 90 days but enterprise add-on for 2 years. We'll include pricing for extended retention.
[14:30] Priya: Anything else on compliance — SOC 2, ISO?
[14:36] Maya: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II, and we have ISO docs in our security pack. We'll attach those to the redline email.
[15:05] Sarah: One procurement nit — can you confirm insurance and indemnity language lines? We need to show the carrier and limit.
[15:14] Maya: Yes we'll include our insurance carrier summary and typical indemnity language; legal can propose counter if needed.
[16:00] Tom: Regarding subprocessor updates — quarterly is fine but we want a notice period for new subprocessors and an objection mechanism.
[16:08] Maya: We can do quarterly updates and a 30-day notice for new subprocessors with an ability to object. We'll scope the mechanism in the DPA.
[16:45] Liam: Operational question: what's the onboarding timeline — how quickly can we be live for the pilot once contracts signed?
[16:53] Carlos: Typically 2 weeks to onboard: account setup, SSO, sample dataset ingest, and one performance tune. If you need dedicated GPU pool it might be 3-4 weeks depending on capacity and region.
[17:21] Priya: Ok — 2 weeks fine. We'll aim for March 9-13 kickoff depending on signatures.
[18:00] Maya: Next up, price approval process — Sarah, do you need a formal quote doc?
[18:08] Sarah: Yes, procurement needs an approved quote with term details to sign off.
[18:15] Maya: We'll produce an approved quote and worksheet and highlight the delta for dedicated vs hosted.
[19:05] Carlos: I'll also attach a benchmark spreadsheet showing latencies at different sequence lengths and a sample SLO dashboard link (note: link shared in chat).
[19:40] Tom: A quick point on breach notification — the 48 hour initial notif is ok, but we want a commitment on escalation to CISO within 24 hours after severity classification.
[19:53] Maya: Ok we'll add that escalation clause.
[20:30] Priya: For the pilot data flow, on privacy we need a flow diagram — who will have access to raw PII?
[20:38] Carlos: We'll provide the data flow diagram; by default engineering/ops with RBAC limited access; in Private deployment you control access.
[21:10] Sarah: Any open procurement blockers? From our side it's mainly legal redline and internal pricing approval.
[21:18] Maya: We'll prioritize the MSA/DPA redline and pricing worksheet.
[22:00] Carlos: Quick note — we can provide a short performance runbook for your engineers to tune batch sizes and caching to meet latency targets.
[22:08] Liam: Great, we'll want that.
[22:45] Tom: On the indemnity cap discussion — please send typical range so legal can evaluate.
[22:51] Maya: We'll include typical indemnity language and ranges in the redline.
[23:20] Sarah: Anything else we should document?
[23:28] Priya: One ask — we'd like to see a run-of-production SLA for sustained throughput (e.g., sustained 50 RPS). Does Redwood publish per-route throughput?
[23:37] Carlos: We publish throughput profiles and can create a per-route SLO for dedicated pools. We'll add that to the appendix.
[24:15] Maya: Ok to recap next steps — we'll send the MSA/DPA redline, SLA appendix, pricing worksheet, security pack, and benchmark spreadsheet. You'll get those by EOD Tuesday.
[24:30] Sarah: Sounds good.
[24:40] Tom: We'll aim to return DPA comments by 2026-02-27.
[24:50] Priya: We'll confirm pilot data access and eval set by 2026-03-03.
[25:02] Maya: Great — thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule the kickoff once signatures are in.
[25:18] (meeting continued with brief Q&A, minor crosstalk and one dropped phrase around 32:10 where audio glitch replaced K-V cache with K-V cash)
[32:10] Carlos: ...so after warmup the KV cache will keep per-request latency low but warmup window depends on traffic pattern.
[36:05] Liam: Re: billing detail, can we get example invoice lines?
[36:15] Maya: Yes we'll add sample invoice lines in the quote package.
[40:00] Sarah: Thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity.
[43:10] Carlos: I'll drop the sample dashboard link and the benchmark CSV in the follow-up.
[47:00] Maya: Final check — any blockers for the legal team to proceed?
[47:10] Tom: Nothing major beyond the redlines we discussed.
[50:00] Priya: We'll try to get the approvals internally; if any speed bumps we'll ping Maya.
[52:00] Maya: Thanks all, call adjourned.
